text: Name a book about AI or machine learning
note: Textbooks, popular science, or fiction where AI is central. Common nicknames count (Bishop, ESL, the Deep Learning book)

answers.a: You Look Like a Thing and I Love You
answers.q: Janelle Shane's book, titled after a neural net's attempt at a pickup line.
Bishop's 1995 book, before PRML made him a one-word citation.
Pearl, 1988. Bayesian networks begin here.

answers.a: Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing

aka: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges
answers.q: The proto-book that unifies CNNs, GNNs and transformers through symmetry, with 5 Gs in its subtitle.

answers.a: Data Mining: Practical Machine Learning Tools and Techniques

answers.q: Toby Segaran, 2007. Many people's first recommender system, written in Python 2.

aka: Probabilistic Programming and Bayesian Methods for Hackers

answers.a: Genetic Algorithms in Search, Optimization, and Machine Learning
Adaptation in Natural and Artificial Systems

answers.q: Hebb, 1949: cells that fire together wire together, give or take the wording.
Weizenbaum, 1976. ELIZA's creator, alarmed at how people treated ELIZA.

answers.a: The Human Use of Human Beings

answers.q: Brian Christian's account of competing as a human in the Loebner Prize. He won 'Most Human Human'.
George Dyson borrowed the title from Samuel Butler's 1863 letter.
Ted Chiang's novella on raising digital pets for years. Training is parenting.

aka: The Diamond Age: Or, A Young Lady's Illustrated Primer

answers.q: Roz, a robot shipwrecked on an island, raises a gosling. Became a 2024 film.
Butler, 1872: a society that smashed its machines, fearing they would evolve consciousness.
E. M. Forster, 1909. Everyone lives in pods, talks through screens, and worships the Machine.

answers.a: I Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream
answers.q: Harlan Ellison, 1967. AM is very angry.

answers.a: Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
The Nature of Statistical Learning Theory

aka: Multiple View Geometry in Computer Vision

answers.q: Every matrix derivative you'll ever forget, in one PDF. Tacked to many a grad-student wall.

answers.a: The Little Book of Deep Learning
answers.q: François Fleuret's deep learning book, sized and formatted to read on a phone.

answers.a: The Principles of Deep Learning Theory
Deep Learning for Coders with fastai and PyTorch

aka: Machine Learning with PyTorch and Scikit-Learn

answers.a: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)
answers.q: Raschka builds a GPT one chapter at a time, so you finally know where every tensor goes.
Andrew Ng's free book, mailed out a chapter at a time as drafts.

aka: Perceptrons: An Introduction to Computational Geometry
answers.q: Minsky and Papert, 1969. The XOR problem, and the book often blamed for the first neural-net winter.
Rumelhart and McClelland's 1986 volumes. Backprop's coming-out party.

aka: Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine

answers.q: Dreyfus, 1972. AI researchers hated it. Some of it aged well.
Penrose argues minds aren't algorithms. Quantum microtubules are involved.

answers.a: Artificial Intelligence: A Guide for Thinking Humans

answers.q: Cade Metz on deep learning's rise, including the 2012 auction for Hinton's three-person startup.

answers.a: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
answers.q: Yudkowsky and Soares, 2025. The title is the summary.
Karen Hao's 2025 book on OpenAI.

aka: The Age of AI: And Our Human Future
Hello World: Being Human in the Age of Algorithms

answers.q: Anil Ananthaswamy's 2024 tour of the math behind ML, from perceptrons to transformers.
Clarke wrote the novel alongside Kubrick's film. HAL is just as polite on paper.

answers.a: The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress
answers.q: Heinlein, 1966. Mike, a lunar computer, wakes up and helps run a revolution.
Ishiguro's 2021 novel narrated by an Artificial Friend who worships the sun.
A security android hacks its governor module and uses the freedom to binge-watch TV.
Stanisław Lem's robot fables. One machine can make anything starting with 'n', including nothing.
Karel Čapek's 1920 play gave us the word 'robot', from the Czech for forced labour.
ESL's friendlier little sibling, now with a Python edition.
Sutton and Barto. The second edition is free, and everyone has read chapter 6.
Pedro Domingos's quest for one learner to rule them all. Xi Jinping reportedly had it on his shelf.

aka: Human Compatible: AI and the Problem of Control

answers.q: Judea Pearl on causality: correlation might not be causation, but here's a ladder.

answers.a: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
aka: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep
answers.q: Philip K. Dick, 1968. Became Blade Runner, sheep mostly omitted.
Gibson, 1984. Made 'cyberspace' famous. Wintermute just wants to merge.
François Chollet, creator of Keras, teaching Keras. Shocking.
Andriy Burkov's slim book. The hundred pages are approximate.

answers.a: Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms
answers.q: David MacKay's free book, with marginal cartoons and a lot of heart.

aka: Gödel Escher Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid
answers.q: Hofstadter's Pulitzer winner. Owned by many, finished by a strange loop of few.
Bostrom, 2014. Musk tweeted about it, and the paperclips went mainstream.
Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, 2016. Free online, and heavy enough to stop a door.
Used in over 1,500 universities. Weighs about as much as a small robot.
Bishop, 2006. Taught a generation to love plate notation and fear Chapter 10.
The free PDF everyone downloaded and few finished.

aka: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras and TensorFlow
answers.q: Aurélien Géron's practitioner's bible. The cover has a fire salamander.
Asimov's 1950 collection, home of the Three Laws and the many ways they go wrong.
